questions.learningObjective: Explain why a rational function is discontinuous
questions.stem: A rational function is discontinuous where its denominator is zero. Why?

answer.exemplar: Division by zero is undefined, so the function has no value at those points, breaking continuity even if the numerator is finite.

questions.explanation: A zero denominator makes the function undefined at that point, which violates the continuity requirement that f(a) exist.
questions.hint: What does division by zero mean?

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a one-sided limit of a step function
questions.stem: For a step function that jumps from 1 to 3 at x = 2, evaluate the right-hand limit at 2.
questions.explanation: The right-hand limit takes the value on the right side of the jump, which is 3.

questions.subject: CALCULUS_I
questions.learningObjective: Summarize discontinuity classification
questions.stem: Which discontinuity type can be removed by redefining the function at a single point?

options.misconception: a jump cannot be fixed by one point
an asymptote cannot be removed by redefinition

questions.explanation: Only a removable discontinuity can be eliminated by redefining the function at one point; jumps and infinite discontinuities cannot.
